messages:
morgan: quick Q — after the helm merge a few minutes ago tenant namespace uploader pods started CrashLooping with mount errors for the projected token volume. chart values now set serviceAccount.create=false and we reference an existing SA with an IRSA annotation. anyone seen the same?

alex: saw it. Root cause was the chart patch that removed `automountServiceAccountToken` and the projected volume section in the podSpec. CI passed but runtime fails. Repro: `kubectl describe pod uploader-... -n tenant-ns` shows `MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "token" : secret not found` (projected token not created).

morgan: ahh makes sense. we manage that SA via terraform (modules/tenant/service_account). do we need to add the annotation there or change helm values?

alex: do both — terraform should own the SA annotation for IRSA role binding, helm should not be forcing automount=false. In TF we usually have: 
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "uploader" {
  metadata {
    name = var.name
    namespace = var.namespace
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = var.role_arn
    }
  }
  automount_service_account_token = true
}
```
That ensures the SA is annotated and will allow projected token to be created.

jin: FYI I rolled the release back to v1.3.2 in the tenant chart so prod is stable again. But we should patch master chart/values and TF before next deploy.

tara: confirmed adding `automount_service_account_token = true` in TF fixed the uploader in staging for me. Also had to patch the pod to use the projected volume mount, e.g.:
```yaml
volumes:
  - name: token
    projected:
      sources:
        - serviceAccountToken:
            audience: sts.amazonaws.com
            expirationSeconds: 3600
            path: token
```
and then mount `/var/run/secrets/tokens/token` in the container.

morgan: good notes. two follow-ups: 1) should we set expirationSeconds != 0? what's our recommendation for IRSA use here (init container vs long lived process)? 2) will changing TF SA metadata trigger pod restarts/rolling updates?

alex: 1) expirationSeconds=3600 is safe (1h) for most workloads. If you need longer lived tokens use refresh logic; don't set to 0 unless you really want a permanent token. 2) updating SA annotations does not automatically restart pods; pods only see token projection when they are recreated or if the projected token is refreshed by kubelet. For a sure fix we patch the deployment to force a rollout (kubectl rollout restart deploy/uploader -n tenant-ns) after SA fix.

morgan: ok i'll open a PR to the terraform module to add the annotation + automount flag and a separate PR to chart values to stop setting automount=false. i'll include a rollout restart step in the release notes. pinging @eng-infra for review once PRs are up. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: CI for terraform-modules/tenant#432 passed — plan shows adding annotation to kubernetes_service_account.uploader (no other changes).

jin: nice — once PR merged run `kubectl rollout restart` for tenant-ns deployments and monitor tokens in pods with `ls -l /var/run/secrets/tokens` and `cat /var/run/secrets/tokens/token | base64 --decode` for quick sanity check.

morgan: thanks all — will link PRs here in 10m and add a short runbook note about projected token paths and the need to restart deployments after SA annotation changes.

tara: one more: if anyone hits AWS IAM role mismatch after annotation update, double-check the role ARN is correct and that OIDC provider thumbprint + trust policy are in place. we had a mismatch last month and it looked like token problem but was IAM deny.

morgan: good call. i'll include a checklist in the PR template. closing this thread once PRs merged.
